levels.title: Keep the Craft, Improve the Use
levels.focus: understand design facts and infer why tradition and innovation are combined
levels.outcome: Identify the retained and changed features, then infer why makers used both from the stated outcome.

connect.teaching_block: A careful design decision can preserve a recognisable cultural feature while improving safety, comfort, durability, or use.
connect.passage: A pottery group kept its regional painted border but changed to a lead-free glaze.
connect.prompt: The border is the retained tradition; the safer glaze is the innovation; both clues are needed for the inference.

co_construct.teaching_block: Use a retain-change-outcome map so innovation is neither praised blindly nor treated as the destruction of tradition. Work through the first decision with the clue named before the response.
co_construct.passage: Design record from a bangle studio: the team kept a familiar floral border; it added a lightweight clasp for comfort; customers recognised the craft but found it easier to wear.
co_construct.prompt: Which statement correctly separates the retained feature, the innovation, and the stated outcome? Work through one clue and test it against every possible response.
options: Retained: added a lightweight clasp for comfort; changed: kept a familiar floral border; outcome: none.
Retained: kept a familiar floral border; changed: added a lightweight clasp for comfort; outcome: customers recognised the craft but found it easier to wear.
Every traditional feature was removed and no outcome was stated.
The outcome happened before either design decision.
accepted_answers: Retained: kept a familiar floral border; changed: added a lightweight clasp for comfort; outcome: customers recognised the craft but found it easier to wear.
